name: T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B cell lymphoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues

criteria.description: Presence of scattered large neoplastic B cells in a background rich in reactive T cells and histiocytes
Neoplastic cells positive for B-cell markers (CD20, CD79a) with abundant reactive T cells (CD3+) and histiocytes
Exclusion of classical diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and nodular lymphocyte predominant Hodgkin lymphoma
Lymphadenopathy with or without systemic B symptoms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of large B cells in a T-cell/histiocyte-rich background with immunophenotypic evidence and exclusion of other lymphoma subtypes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of morphology, immunophenotyping, and clinical features.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically involves cervical, axillary, or inguinal nodes

pathognomonic.symptomName: B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)

common.notes: Enlargement of liver and spleen due to infiltration
Marker of tumor burden and cell turnover
Secondary to bone marrow involvement or chronic disease
searchTerms: fatigue related to low red blood cells

occasional.notes: May cause anemia, thrombocytopenia, or leukopenia
searchTerms: bone marrow affected causing low blood cells
bone marrow disease with blood cell loss

laboratory: Anemia and other cytopenias in peripheral blood
Presence of large atypical B cells on flow cytometry
imaging: CT scan demonstrating nodal and extranodal involvement
genetic: No specific recurrent genetic abnormalities; complex karyotypes may be present
other: Histopathology showing scattered large B cells in a background rich in reactive T cells and histiocytes

distinguishingFeatures: More uniform large B-cell population without prominent reactive T-cell/histiocyte background

redFlags: Unexplained persistent fever and night sweats
